key_insight: Accounting for temperature-dependent water properties through calibrated profile transformations predicts turbulent friction and heat transfer within 2% of DNS, except at the lowest Reynolds numbers.
engineering_relevance: Variable-property modeling can improve heated or cooled water-channel design, where constant-property assumptions and empirical correlations can produce substantial errors.
method: Run plane-channel DNS with temperature-dependent viscosity and conductivity under wall heating and cooling.
Derive integral mean-profile transformations from momentum and energy balances, calibrating eddy-viscosity and diffusivity corrections against DNS.
Apply the same corrections to the Spalart–Allmaras turbulence model.
evidence_signal: Across wall temperatures of 277–360 K and wall Prandtl numbers of 2–12, friction changed by −39% to +32% versus constant-property flow, empirical correlations deviated by up to 26%, and corrected Spalart–Allmaras modeling halved its friction error.
watch_item: The corrections are DNS-calibrated for constant-density plane-channel water flow, and prediction accuracy deteriorates at the lowest Reynolds numbers.
paper_title: Direct numerical simulation of turbulent heat transfer in water with temperature-dependent viscosity and conductivity
